# Lab runs kept in the repository

The raw files of the lab runs behind the committed evidence, as the lab wrote them: the runner's results, the artifacts it collected and the exported telemetry. `rasd evidence --check`, a step of `rasd ci`, reads them again on every build and fails unless each `evidence.md` that cites one is, byte for byte, what `rasd evidence` writes from it today, with today's rules. A rule edited until it no longer fires on its lab run loses its evidence in the same build.

A run is kept only when everything in it may be public: machines that existed for the run, accounts that mean nothing. A run made on your own lab VMs stays with you ([Privacy](../../red/lab/README.md)); its evidence is then taken as written, and listed at the end of this page.

## hosted-44858268614

GitHub-hosted runners (windows-2022 and ubuntu-24.04), each marked as a RASD lab host for one run and discarded after it. No domain. A Splunk Enterprise stood beside each lab host for the run, started by a person who accepted its terms, with the RASD apps in it and no vendor add-on; the siem.json of each part says which Splunk it was.
